newsitem.title: USA: AES to build 600 MW Brazilian power plant.
newsitem.headline: AES to build 600 MW Brazilian power plant.

text.p: AES Corp said on Wednesday that Companhia Estadual de Energia Eletrica (CEEE) has selected the company to build, own and operate a 600 megawatt, gas-fired power plant in Brazil.
The plant will sell electricity to CEEE for 20 years under a contract, which is expected to be signed soon, AES said.
AES said the plant will be located near the border city of Uruguaiana and natural gas will be supplied to the plant from Argentina through an expansion of the Argentine northern pipeline system.
Financial terms of the deal were not immediately available.
AES expects to begin construction in 1997 and to commence base-load commercial operations in 1999, it said.
AES also said that Hazel O'Leary, the former U.S. secretary of energy under President Clinton, will be joining AES's board of directors in April 1997.
O'Leary was previously a member of the AES board of directors from 1988 to 1989, before taking an executive position with Northern States Power Co of Minnesota.
Liz Gusmati, AES manager of business affairs, said the investment for the Brazilian power plant is expected to be about $320 million.
